answer: Persistent Provenance Ledger. Every agent identity embeds a grove-specific random seed in a hardware enclave that signs each transaction with a monotonically increasing counter. A voyage across registries leaves a signed chain other nodes verify. Minting a duplicate forces replaying that counter chain, and any fork reveals two signed histories for one seed. Attackers must acquire distinct enclave seeds per identity at real hardware cost, roughly one physical chip per sybil, and fresh nectar accrues only to the oldest verified chain.
